case_study.title: Discovery & Prototyping Hub
case_study.subtitle: From Figma to live code: a prototyping platform bridging design, AI, and development to validate experiences before writing production code.

problem.title: The Problem
problem.p1: In complex digital products — especially in HealthTech, where a web platform for operators coexists with mobile apps for professionals, patients, and drivers — the classic design flow creates critical frictions:
problem.li1: Static prototypes do not reflect real complexity. A Figma mockup cannot simulate loading states, real-time validations, or multi-step flows with dynamic data.
problem.li2: Handoff is a bottleneck. Developers receive PDFs or Figma links that do not match the real frontend component architecture.
problem.li3: Documentation becomes outdated at the first change. Specifications written in parallel to the prototype are rewritten with each iteration.
problem.li4: UX testing is expensive and slow. Coordinating sessions with real users for each iteration is unsustainable in agile cycles.

beforeAfter.title: Before vs. After
beforeAfter.desc: The impact of the Discovery Hub compared to the traditional design flow.

items.before: Design in Figma → PDF specs → Dev interprets
items.after: Live code prototype → Auto-derived spec → Dev implements

items.before: Manual testing every 2 weeks with real users
Handoff in ~2 weeks of manual documentation
items.after: Handoff in 1 day (automated derivation with skills)

items.before: Manual docs that get outdated on first change
items.after: Living docs with automated verification scripts

items.before: Prototypes that dont match dev architecture
items.after: Same stack as production: React, MUI, TypeScript

solution.title: The Solution
solution.desc: A prototyping monorepo that replicates the real development stack, fueled with mock data, where every feature is designed, validated, and documented before writing a single line of production code.

cards.title: Cross-Platform Monorepo
cards.desc: 4 environments (1 web + 3 mobile) with the same stack as production. Shared components, centralized mock data, and independent playgrounds per platform.

cards.title: Discoveries System
cards.desc: Every feature is a "Discovery" — a functional unit grouping components, pages, hooks, mocks, and docs. 15+ discoveries completed.

cards.title: AI Skills (Claude Code)
cards.desc: 3 skills that automate the cycle: discovery-start, handoff, and synth-run. From initial research to development team handoff.

cards.title: Synthetic Users
cards.desc: Fictional personas with YAML profiles that navigate prototypes and report UX friction in 3 layers. 30+ tests executed automatically.

cards.title: Spec-Driven Development
cards.desc: Two doc families that never merge: the narrative (the why) and the norm (the what). Automated verification scripts.

cards.title: Frictionless Handoff
cards.desc: Developers receive functional prototypes in their exact stack, specifications derived from code, and test cases.

architecture.title: Monorepo Architecture
architecture.desc: A single repository containing the 4 product environments, with centralized shared resources.

hero.title: B2B App for Buyers
hero.subtitle: Digitization and optimization of the inventory purchasing process for supermarkets, eliminating paper use and improving communication with suppliers.

about.title: About the Project
about.desc: A supermarket with a strong presence in Spain needed to modernize how its buyers replenish stock for different stores. Currently, all processes are done on paper (note-taking, quotes, delivery notes) and then the information must be transcribed to a desktop PC.

problem.title: The Problem
problem.desc: The current process at Mercabarna was extremely inefficient and prone to human errors:
items: Information loss due to losing papers with price notes and quotes.
Wasted time walking around the whole premises to find suppliers or information.
Errors when transcribing information from paper to the system at the end of the day.
Lack of tools to document product status (e.g., broken pallets) in real time.

research.title: Research & Discovery
research.desc: We conducted interviews with current buyers to understand their workflow, frustrations, and technological needs. This allowed us to create two key user personas and map their current journey.

personas.name: Juan Carlos
personas.quote: I really enjoy my job, negotiate and talk with people is the best!
personas.bio: Juan Carlos is an Accountant, he has been working as buyer for 8 years. He really enjoys his job and does it always with a smile. After work he comes home to spend time with his family.
needs: Don't lose contact with his suppliers.
Stay on his position until his retirement.
frustrations: Don't spend too many time with his family because of work.
Long walks over Mercabarna to do his job.

personas.name: Martin Cuevas
personas.quote: Everyday is a new challenge, I'll do my best to grow on my career
personas.bio: Martin has a Degree on Business Administration. He works as buyer for a supermarket with a strong presence throughout Spain. After work he likes relaxing and going out with his friends.
needs: Apply technology that would help him on his job.
frustrations: He feels that He wastes time the way he works.
He easily loses the papers where He makes notations.

define.title: Define
needs: Create an environment to communicate with suppliers without losing any information in the middle.
A method to easily integrate order in the actual workflow.
Easier access to old interactions to make new purchases.
Digitalize the process... more synced with system for checking the stock (++).

touchpoints: Warehouse manager has to wait until order comes, without information (Negative point)
Rewrite info from paper to PC

userflow.title: Userflow
userflow.desc: The diagram shows the complexity of the purchasing process from checking the stock to sending the invoice to administration.

decisions.text: Is the order information correct? If not, the flow requires editing the order by changing quantities or deleting products before sending it to the supplier.
Is the order okay upon arrival? If there are problems, the flow requires reporting the issue by issuing a form before starting another order.

visual_design.title: Visual Design
visual_design.s1_desc: Here we provide a list of all Supermarket's Suppliers, with important information like phone number and local number where they are located.
visual_design.s2_desc: Once we select a supplier, the next screen show us a Control Panel, where we can handle different information about that supplier.
visual_design.s3_desc: Items catalog where we can find every product that the Supermarket buys and his current stock on warehouse. Then we can enter agreed price and quantity while negotiate.
visual_design.s3_extra: Also, there is the possibility to edit the order after compare all offers. The order list is unique for each supplier.
visual_design.s4_desc: When something is wrong with the order we provide a quick form which is sent to supplier, also we keep a copy who is stored on Supplier's Control Panel to gather information about that kind of problems.
visual_design.s5_desc: On this screen, we provide stock information about all products on the list. With visual aids that advice when some product is low stock for example.
visual_design.s6_desc: Integrated chat for easy contact with suppliers who are using the App if they need to resolve any problem or negotiate some prices.
